title: Introduction to CodeIgniter Models
description: A beginner-friendly walkthrough of what Models are for, how to create the file, how to load one, and how to set up the database connection.
congratsText: You've got the fundamentals of CodeIgniter Models!
objectives: Explain what a Model is responsible for in a CodeIgniter application
Create a Model file that follows CodeIgniter's naming and structure rules
Load a Model inside a Controller so its methods become available
Configure the database connection settings a Model needs in order to run
recap: A Model holds the data logic — the database work lives there, not in the Controller
Model files sit in application/models, start with a capital letter, and extend CI_Model
$this->load->model('name') makes a Model available as $this->name inside a Controller
Your database hostname, username, password, and name are set in config/database.php

chunks.text: A Model is the part of your app that deals with data — usually reading from and writing to the database.

check.question: What does a Model mainly deal with?

chunks.text: Keeping database code in the Model means your Controller stays short and easy to read.
If two different pages need the same list of students, both can call the same Model method instead of repeating the query.

check.question: Can several Controllers reuse one Model?

quiz.question: What is a Model responsible for in a CodeIgniter application?
options: Deciding which page layout the browser should end up showing
Handling the data, such as database reads and writes
Receiving the incoming URL request and routing it to a method
Storing the HTML markup that gets displayed to the site visitor

chunks.text: Model files go in the application/models folder, and the filename starts with a capital letter, like Student_model.php.
Inside the file, the class extends CI_Model so it inherits everything CodeIgniter provides.
The class name must match the filename exactly — Student_model.php must contain class Student_model.

check.question: Must the class name match the filename?

quiz.question: Arrange the tokens to declare a Model class correctly.

chunks.text: A Model does nothing until a Controller loads it with $this->load->model('student_model').

check.question: What must happen before you use a Model?

chunks.text: Once loaded, the Model becomes available as a property — you reach it with $this->student_model.

check.question: After loading, how do you reach the Model?

chunks.text: Forgetting to load it gives an undefined property error, which is the most common beginner mistake here.

quiz.question: Which line belongs on the comment line so this code works?

chunks.text: Before a Model can read any table, CodeIgniter needs your connection details, and those live in application/config/database.php.

check.question: Which file holds the connection details?

chunks.text: You fill in four settings inside $db['default']: hostname, username, password, and database.
On a normal WAMP setup the hostname is localhost and the username is root — a wrong value here gives a connection error.
